candidate.title: CIRS-seq
candidate.scope: The assigned CIRS-seq poster row: protein-associated, in vivo folded RNA is deproteinized and probed in two separate chemical-treatment branches, then reverse transcribed and hydrolyzed to yield branch-specific cDNA. The unlabeled upper branch is interpreted as CMCT using the 2014 primary paper; the lower branch is labeled DMS. Neighboring icSHAPE and SHAPE-MaP rows and the clipped SHAPE-Seq caption are visible context, not alternative targets of the CIRS-seq row. This is the native deproteinized RNA implementation, not the unshown 2′-O-methylation adaptation. The drawing ends at cDNA; the paper clarifies its downstream library/readout interface without supplying additional drawn operations.

operations.label: Proteinase K treatment
operations.description: Remove RNA-associated proteins, producing RNA in native deproteinized conformation while retaining the depicted hairpin. The primary paper places this step in cell lysate.
operations.mechanism: Proteinase K treatment unmasks protein-bound RNA regions.
operations.information_effect: Changes accessibility to the chemical probes: the target is native deproteinized RNA structure, including regions previously masked by proteins.

evidence.locator: CIRS-seq row, left: label, hairpin icon, blue protein-associated RNA and Proteinase K treatment arrow

evidence.quote: To perform transcriptome-wide probing of RNAs in their native deproteinized conformation, we lysed mouse ESCs in an isotonic buffer, and treated the lysate with Proteinase K to unmask regions of RNAs bound by proteins, without affecting the RNA structure (supplementary Materials and methods in Additional file 1).

operations.label: Reaction
operations.description: Chemically modify accessible residues of the deproteinized RNA in the unlabeled upper branch, assigned to CMCT from the primary paper.
operations.mechanism: CMCT primarily forms adducts with pseudouridine N1/N3 and uridine N3, and less strongly with guanosine/inosine N1; the primary paper resolves the unlabeled upper reaction.
operations.information_effect: Introduces covalent chemical marks associated with accessible, preferentially unpaired positions; the marks are not sequence barcodes. Reactivity is not perfect specificity for a unique secondary structure.

evidence.locator: CIRS-seq row, upper branch: arrow to modified loop, reverse transcription, RNA hydrolysis and upper cDNA

evidence.quote: The CIRS-seq method (Figure 1) is based on the use of DMS, which mainly methylates N1 of adenosine and N3 of cytosine [36,37], and CMCT, which primarily forms adducts with N1 and N3 of pseudouridine, N3 of uridine, and, to a lesser extent, N1 of guanosine and inosine [38-40] but only when these residues are in single-stranded conformation.
Despite the respective strong preference of DMS and CMCT for A/C and G/U residues, we also observed non-canonical reactivities in both treatments.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Use the CMCT-modified RNA as template to synthesize cDNA; modification-induced RT termination converts RNA chemical accessibility into cDNA end positions.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper reports random-primed RT and modification-induced stopping one nucleotide downstream of the modified residue.
operations.information_effect: The physical signal carrier becomes the cDNA end associated with the RNA sequence. Natural RT stops can yield similar ends; the paper uses an unshown non-treated control.

operations.label: RNA hydrolysis
operations.description: Remove the RNA template from the CMCT branch reverse-transcription product, leaving cDNA.
operations.mechanism: RNA hydrolysis is explicitly captioned; no hydrolysis reagent or end-group chemistry is specified.
operations.information_effect: Retains the cDNA sequence and termination boundary. The paper reports downstream adapter ligation and Illumina sequencing: mapped RT-stop positions give residue-level reactivity information after accounting for natural stops. These downstream operations are not drawn here.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven local operations belong to the sole assigned target, CIRS-seq. Proteinase K treatment is shared upstream; CMCT and DMS are separate chemical-treatment branches with distinct RT and RNA-hydrolysis instances. The paper identifies the otherwise unlabeled upper treatment as CMCT and describes the native deproteinized lysate implementation. A non-treated control and adapter ligation/sequencing are reported in the paper but are outside the drawn route. The neighboring named poster rows do not establish grouped applicability. Chemical accessibility supports inference of unpaired positions and structure constraints; it does not directly identify all base pairs or guarantee a unique structure.

evidence.quote: To perform transcriptome-wide probing of RNAs in their native deproteinized conformation, we lysed mouse ESCs in an isotonic buffer, and treated the lysate with Proteinase K to unmask regions of RNAs bound by proteins, without affecting the RNA structure (supplementary Materials and methods in Additional file 1).

The CIRS-seq method (Figure 1) is based on the use of DMS, which mainly methylates N1 of adenosine and N3 of cytosine [36,37], and CMCT, which primarily forms adducts with N1 and N3 of pseudouridine, N3 of uridine, and, to a lesser extent, N1 of guanosine and inosine [38-40] but only when these residues are in single-stranded conformation.

Treatment of RNA with the two reagents enables the detection of unpaired nucleotide positions due to the modification-induced reverse transcription (RT) stop one nucleotide downstream of the modified residue.
Extracted RNA was subjected to random-primed RT. A non-treated control was also produced to determine naturally occurring RT stops.
The generated cDNAs were adapter ligated and subjected to high-throughput sequencing using the Illumina platform
Mapping reads to the transcriptome provide information regarding how many RT stops occurred at each position of the analyzed transcripts.
Despite the respective strong preference of DMS and CMCT for A/C and G/U residues, we also observed non-canonical reactivities in both treatments.
Constraints derived from chemical probing data may significantly improve the accuracy of RNA secondary structure prediction tools [42,56].
evidence.rationale: The measured quantity is chemical reactivity inferred from cDNA stops. Its use as a constraint for structure prediction supports treating the assay as indirect evidence about accessible/unpaired positions, rather than a direct enumeration of RNA base pairs.

evidence.quote: Genome-wide profiling of mouse RNA secondary structures reveals key features of the mammalian transcriptome.

To perform transcriptome-wide probing of RNAs in their native deproteinized conformation, we lysed mouse ESCs in an isotonic buffer, and treated the lysate with Proteinase K to unmask regions of RNAs bound by proteins, without affecting the RNA structure (supplementary Materials and methods in Additional file 1).

The CIRS-seq method (Figure 1) is based on the use of DMS, which mainly methylates N1 of adenosine and N3 of cytosine [36,37], and CMCT, which primarily forms adducts with N1 and N3 of pseudouridine, N3 of uridine, and, to a lesser extent, N1 of guanosine and inosine [38-40] but only when these residues are in single-stranded conformation.

Treatment of RNA with the two reagents enables the detection of unpaired nucleotide positions due to the modification-induced reverse transcription (RT) stop one nucleotide downstream of the modified residue.
